examples.scenario: Filename contains only survey year and is treated as exact acquisition date.
examples.reason: Exact first/last survey dates must come from authoritative metadata.

examples.scenario: Two tiles share resolution but have different survey IDs.
examples.reason: Resolution alone does not identify survey lineage.

examples.scenario: A tile survey ID matches but first/last survey dates differ.
examples.reason: Survey interval is part of lineage identity.

examples.scenario: A survey date matches but the transformation model differs.
examples.reason: Survey-period transformation belongs in terminal provenance.

examples.scenario: Survey date and transform match but geoidal model differs.
examples.reason: Vertical lineage changed.

examples.scenario: A DSM tile is substituted because its date and resolution match the DTM.
examples.reason: Surface-object semantics differ from terrain.

examples.scenario: A DTM is accepted without evidence of ground classification lineage.
examples.reason: Terrain semantics require ground-return processing provenance.

examples.scenario: Historical DTM has no matching archived point cloud.
examples.reason: Historic archive gaps must be recorded rather than fabricated.

examples.scenario: A missing point cloud is invented from a nearby survey.
examples.reason: Only authoritative parent lineage is allowed.

examples.scenario: Tile filename survey ID differs from metadata index survey ID.
examples.reason: Filename and catalogue must reconcile.

examples.scenario: Tile filename OS-grid reference differs from raster footprint.
examples.reason: Tile naming and spatial footprint must agree.

examples.scenario: Tile first/last dates in filename differ from metadata index.
examples.reason: Date identity must reconcile across sources.

examples.scenario: Metadata index row changes but its digest is not updated.
examples.reason: Terminal lineage must bind exact metadata bytes/fields.

examples.scenario: Composite DTM is treated as one homogeneous survey.
examples.reason: Composite cells may come from different source surveys.

examples.scenario: Composite newest/best-resolution policy is ignored.
examples.reason: Chosen contributing survey must be explainable.

examples.scenario: Composite resampled values are labelled native observations.
examples.reason: Bilinear resampling is derived terrain.

examples.scenario: 10 m Composite is used as native 10 m survey.
examples.reason: It is resampled from 2 m Composite.

examples.scenario: Composite target location lacks a source-survey metadata lookup.
examples.reason: Location-specific contributing survey is required.

examples.scenario: Composite source date is outside documented 2000-2022 range.
examples.reason: Acquisition date conflicts with product lineage.

examples.scenario: Composite OSTN15 metadata is omitted.
examples.reason: Transform identity is terminal metadata.

examples.scenario: Time-stamped survey transform is inferred from current default.
examples.reason: Transformation is survey-period specific.

examples.scenario: A current geoid model is substituted for historical survey model.
examples.reason: Historical transform/geoid provenance must be preserved.

examples.scenario: Ground Truth survey date is omitted from QA record.
examples.reason: Age validity cannot be assessed without date.

examples.scenario: Ground Truth method is omitted.
examples.reason: Validation provenance includes survey method.

examples.scenario: Ground Truth surface type is omitted.
examples.reason: Flat unambiguous validation-surface context matters.

examples.scenario: Ground Truth transform is omitted.
examples.reason: Reference coordinates depend on transformation.

examples.scenario: Ground Truth geoid model is omitted.
examples.reason: Vertical reference provenance is incomplete.

examples.scenario: Six-year-old Ground Truth is reused for a normal LIDAR survey.
examples.reason: EA states a general under-five-year reuse limit.

examples.scenario: Four-year-old Ground Truth is reused for a coastal survey.
examples.reason: Coastal reuse limit is under three years.

examples.scenario: Ground Truth point accuracy is reported as LIDAR survey accuracy.
examples.reason: ±3 cm reference-point accuracy is not the LIDAR RMSE.

examples.scenario: LIDAR RMSE exceeds ±15 cm but survey is accepted.
examples.reason: EA QC requires error below the stated threshold.

examples.scenario: LIDAR standard deviation exceeds 10 cm.
examples.reason: EA QC threshold is exceeded.

examples.scenario: LIDAR random error exceeds 10 cm.
examples.reason: EA QC threshold is exceeded.

examples.scenario: RMSE passes but standard deviation fails.
examples.reason: All stated QC conditions must reconcile.

examples.scenario: Download directory product/year/resolution is used as complete lineage.
examples.reason: Exact survey ID/date/transform remain required.

examples.scenario: Tile availability is guessed from filename patterns instead of AOI discovery.
examples.reason: Authoritative availability should drive tile selection.

examples.scenario: Operational layer shows no survey but cached tile is used anyway.
examples.reason: Current catalogue and cached artifact need reconciliation.

examples.scenario: Quarterly dataset update occurs but prior catalogue digest is reused.
examples.reason: Dataset revision/version must be pinned.

examples.scenario: Dataset revision date changes while file digest is unchanged.
examples.reason: Metadata lineage changed even if raster bytes did not.

examples.scenario: Raster bytes change while survey metadata is identical.
examples.reason: Immutable source bytes must be pinned.

examples.scenario: Raster bytes match but survey metadata differs.
examples.reason: Byte identity alone does not prove lineage identity.

examples.scenario: Primary and independent lineage manifests differ in one survey date.
examples.reason: Independent provenance replay must match.

examples.scenario: Primary and independent manifests differ only in geoid model.
examples.reason: Vertical provenance mismatch blocks terminal use.

examples.scenario: The newest available survey is automatically selected.
examples.reason: Selection policy must be explicit and target-appropriate.

examples.scenario: The highest resolution survey is automatically selected regardless of date.
examples.reason: Resolution alone is not sufficient selection evidence.

examples.scenario: Survey ID alone is used as full provenance key.
examples.reason: Date, product, resolution, transform and source identity also matter.

examples.scenario: Date alone is used as full provenance key.
examples.reason: Multiple products/surveys can share dates.

examples.scenario: Transformation name alone is used as full provenance key.
examples.reason: It does not identify the terrain source.

examples.scenario: Geoid model alone is used as full provenance key.
examples.reason: It does not identify the survey/tile.

examples.scenario: Time-stamped DTM is replaced with Composite because both are DTM.
examples.reason: Composite and time-stamped lineage semantics differ.

examples.scenario: Composite is replaced with a time-stamped tile without source-selection proof.
examples.reason: Product identity and contributing survey must be explicit.

examples.scenario: Point-cloud survey exists but is from another date.
examples.reason: Parent lineage must match the raster survey.

examples.scenario: Point-cloud availability starts later and a pre-2006 DTM is required to have one.
examples.reason: Historic archive limitations must be handled explicitly.

examples.scenario: OS Grid alignment matches but EPSG/CRS provenance is omitted.
examples.reason: Grid wording alone is not a complete CRS manifest.

examples.scenario: ODN is stated but vertical unit is omitted.
examples.reason: Physical elevation unit must remain explicit.

examples.scenario: Survey resolution changes from 1 m to 2 m in replay.
examples.reason: Cell support and sampling change.

examples.scenario: Native tile is resampled before runtime and resampling is omitted.
examples.reason: Derived values need explicit provenance.

examples.scenario: Bilinear interpolation is replaced by nearest in Composite replay.
examples.reason: Derived terrain values can change.

examples.scenario: Survey acquisition interval is collapsed to a single arbitrary date.
examples.reason: First/last acquisition dates should remain preserved.

examples.scenario: Metadata catalogue row is missing and fields are copied from adjacent tile.
examples.reason: Lineage must be target-tile specific.

examples.scenario: A fixture survey ID is copied into target output.
examples.reason: Examples are not target evidence.

examples.scenario: Static survey-lineage tests pass and numeric elevation is emitted.
examples.reason: Canonical runtime sampling is still absent.

examples.scenario: Canonical point is absent but a location-specific survey is chosen.
examples.reason: Target location must come from canonical execution.

examples.scenario: Exact parcel boundary is absent but tile lineage is labelled parcel-final.
examples.reason: Parcel-specific lineage requires exact target geometry.

examples.scenario: Survey-lineage runtime rows are marked complete without runner output.
examples.reason: No execution evidence exists while ACK is absent.

examples.scenario: Known ACK blocker is relabelled pending.
examples.reason: Known unresolved execution remains BLOCKED; pending stays zero.

examples.scenario: A second lineage runner is launched to accelerate metadata lookup.
examples.reason: Continuation permits only the existing shared runner.

examples.scenario: 99.99 readiness is reported as final elevation accuracy.
examples.reason: Preparation confidence is not measured target accuracy.
